statement.p: For the vector field \vec G = (ye^{xy}+\cos\mathopen{}\left(x+y\right))\,\vec i + (xe^{xy}+\cos\mathopen{}\left(x+y\right))\,\vec j, find the line integral of \vec G along the curve C from the origin along the x-axis to the point (5,0) and then counterclockwise around the circumference of the circle x^2+y^2=25 to the point (5/\sqrt{2},5/\sqrt{2}).

static.solution: \vec G=\nabla(e^{xy}+\sin\mathopen{}\left(x+y\right)), the line integral can be calculated using the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals: \int_c\vec F\cdot d\vec r= e^{xy}+\sin\mathopen{}\left(x+y\right)\bigg|^{(5/\sqrt{2},5/\sqrt{2})}_{(0.0)} =e^{25/2} + \sin(6\sqrt{2}) - 1.
